text: Elizabeth Greer "Beanie" Feldstein, born on June 24, 1993, is an American actress, singer, and comedian. She first gained recognition for her starring roles in the comedy film Neighbors 2: Sorority Rising (2016), the comedy-drama film Lady Bird (2017), and the coming-of-age comedy Booksmart (2019), for which she received a Golden Globe Award nomination for Best Actress in a Motion Picture–Comedy or Musical. Feldstein made her Broadway debut as Minnie Fay in the 2017 revival of Hello, Dolly!, which premiered with previews on March 15, 2017, and opened on April 20, 2017, starring Bette Midler as Dolly Levi; her performance was positively received by critics. She portrayed the lead role of Fanny Brice in the 2022 revival of Funny Girl, for which she earned a Drama League Award nomination for Distinguished Performance, though reviews were mixed to negative, with critics noting she was not a power singer or delivering a Broadway-caliber performance, leading to her departure from the production on September 6, 2022, and replacement by Lea Michele. In 2021, she portrayed Monica Lewinsky in the third season of the FX anthology series Impeachment: American Crime Story. Feldstein was born in Los Angeles, the only daughter of Sharon Lyn (née Chalkin), a costume designer and fashion stylist, and Richard Feldstein, a tour accountant for Guns N' Roses; she is Jewish and the youngest of three children, with older brother actor Jonah Hill and deceased oldest brother Jordan Feldstein (1977–2017), a manager for Maroon 5. Her nanny nicknamed her "Beanie" when she was an infant, and her brothers also used the name. She attended the Harvard-Westlake School in Los Angeles and Stagedoor Manor, a theatre camp in New York, and has been best friends since high school with Ben Platt, a fellow Broadway and film actor. She graduated from Wesleyan University in 2015 with a degree in sociology. Feldstein made her acting debut in 2002 in the ABC comedy series My Wife and Kids, played Megan in the 2012 musical television pilot Madison High, and appeared as a guest in the third season of Netflix's Orange Is the New Black in 2015. In 2015, she played Anna in the comedy film Fan Girl. She starred in the comedy film The Female Brain, which premiered at the LA Film Festival in June 2017, and co-starred in Lady Bird, directed by Greta Gerwig, which earned a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Picture and a Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture. In 2019, she had a recurring role as Jenna in the first season of What We Do in the Shadows, earning positive critical reviews, though she did not return for the second season due to other commitments. She starred in Olivia Wilde's directorial debut, Booksmart, which received widespread critical acclaim and a Golden Globe nomination. She also portrayed Johanna Morrigan in the coming-of-age comedy How to Build a Girl, an adaptation of Caitlin Moran's 2014 novel, which received positive reviews. In 2020, she guest starred as Tess Anderson in the ABC medical drama Grey's Anatomy, a dream she had since childhood, and voiced a support group therapist in The Simpsons episode "Frinkcoin." She performed a cover of "It Takes Two" from Into the Woods with Ben Platt in the television specials Saturday Night Seder and Take Me to the World: A Sondheim 90th Celebration. Feldstein starred in the drama film The Humans, based on Stephen Karam's one-act play. On August 6, 2019, it was announced she would star as Monica Lewinsky in the third season of Impeachment: American Crime Story; on August 29, 2019, it was announced she would star in Richard Linklater's film adaptation of Merrily We Roll Along, shot over twenty years, alongside Ben Platt and Paul Mescal. In September 2022, she was cast in Ethan Coen's Drive-Away Dolls. Feldstein is queer and met English film producer Bonnie-Chance Roberts on the set of How to Build a Girl; they were engaged in June 2022 and married on May 19, 2023.
